doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

title: Sun Ra browsing the Fletcher Henderson section
summary: Sun Ra visited the shop, driven by Danny Thompson, looking at Henderson and Ellington sections but never buying; his clothing.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Am I correct that two significant people came into the Third Street Jazz and Rock, one being your future wife and one being Sun Ra?
What kind of records would Sun Ra have been looking for?

He would look at — he would go to the Fletcher Henderson section first. And then he would go to the Duke Ellington section. But he never bought anything. He just looked. Christian McBride used to come into my store when he was a kid. Okay? When he was a young kid. He would do the same thing. There’s plenty of people that would just go through the stacks and it was a, you know, wanting to see what was happening. I really eventually tried to have every jazz record in print and out of print, cutouts, which were part of my record store. I tried to carry anything that had a shot of selling because to be asked for a record and not have it would be maybe the worst thing that could happen. So yeah, Sun Ra. Danny Thompson would drive Sun Ra down to my store in a big, white Cadillac. Okay? And it was such a trip, you know, to see Sun Ra walk into the store. And it was such a treat for the customers. They would just stand there with their jaws down to the ground, looking at Sun Ra coming in and looking at, you know, at the Fletcher Henderson section.
Was he dressed as we are, as we remember him, in performance garb?

You know Sun Ra never wore jeans. I mean you wouldn’t see Sun Ra in jeans. You wouldn’t want to see Sun Ra in jeans. He had these platform shoes spray painted silver that he used to wear. And that was always cool. And he didn’t have headgear on or anything like that. But it was always Ra-like clothing.
